biography: Dimitri Sedashev's journey began not on the asphalt, but on the windswept moors of Yorkshire. Growing up near Croft Circuit, the roar of engines was the soundtrack to his childhood. Unlike many racers who inherited wealth, Dimitri’s father, a mechanic at a local garage, fuelled his passion with salvaged kart parts and late nights in the shed. His first competitive karting season was a baptism by fire – a spectacular crash at Rowrah that left him with a broken wrist and a fierce determination to master every inch of the track. This early experience instilled in him a defensive, calculated approach to racing, prioritizing consistency over outright aggression. After dominating the local karting scene, Dimitri transitioned to Ginetta Juniors at 17, quickly establishing himself as a rising star. Now at 21, he's competing in the Ginetta GT4 SuperCup, aiming to prove that talent and grit can overcome financial disadvantages, chasing a dream of reaching GT racing's highest echelons.
drivingStyle: Dimitri's driving style is best described as 'calculated defense.' He's not one for daring overtakes or flamboyant slides. Instead, he focuses on precise lines, meticulous braking points, and conserving tire life. He excels at defending his position, often forcing rivals into making mistakes. While some may criticize his lack of raw aggression, Dimitri believes in the long game, accumulating points and consistently finishing races, a strategy that has proven surprisingly effective throughout his career.

rivalries.reason: A clash of styles. Isabelle's aggressive, risk-taking approach constantly clashes with Dimitri's conservative tactics, leading to frequent on-track battles and off-track friction.
Marcus's immense wealth has granted him opportunities that Dimitri has not had, leading to feelings of resentment. Marcus is seen as a talentless rich kid who uses his money to get ahead.

Chloe is a formidable talent with a similar driving style to Dimitri. Their strategic battles are often close and tense, each trying to outsmart the other. This has led to a healthy respect between the two, but also a fierce determination to come out on top.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky wristband his father made for him before every race.
Studies telemetry data for hours before a race, meticulously analyzing every corner and braking point.
Refuses to eat anything but plain pasta with olive oil on race days – a superstition stemming from a particularly successful race early in his career.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being the fastest for a single lap; it's about being the most consistent over the entire race. It's about smarts, not just speed."
careerHighlight: Winning the Ginetta Junior Championship in 2020, after a season-long battle with a significantly better funded rival. He secured the title in the final race with a masterful defensive drive, holding off constant pressure to cross the finish line first.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the first race of the 2021 Ginetta GT4 SuperCup season while battling for the lead. The incident damaged his confidence and set him back in the championship standings.
